answer_text:
We want the smallest prime factor of

\[
N=4^{52}+52^{2013}+2013^{52}.
\]

We test primes in increasing order: \(2,3,5,7,\dots\)

---

### 1. Test \(p=2\)

\[
4^{52} \text{ is even},\qquad 52^{2013} \text{ is even},\qquad 2013^{52} \text{ is odd}.
\]

So

\[
N \equiv \text{even}+\text{even}+\text{odd}\equiv 1 \pmod 2.
\]

Thus \(2\nmid N\).

---

### 2. Test \(p=3\)

Reduce each base modulo \(3\):

\[
4\equiv 1 \pmod 3,\qquad 52\equiv 1 \pmod 3,\qquad 2013\equiv 0 \pmod 3.
\]

Therefore,

\[
N \equiv 1^{52}+1^{2013}+0^{52}\equiv 1+1+0\equiv 2 \pmod 3.
\]

Thus \(3\nmid N\).

---

### 3. Test \(p=5\)

Reduce modulo \(5\):

\[
4\equiv -1 \pmod 5,\qquad 52\equiv 2 \pmod 5,\qquad 2013\equiv 3 \pmod 5.
\]

So

\[
4^{52}\equiv (-1)^{52}\equiv 1 \pmod 5.
\]

Since \(2^4\equiv 1\pmod 5\) and \(2013\equiv 1\pmod 4\),

\[
52^{2013}\equiv 2^{2013}\equiv 2 \pmod 5.
\]

Also \(3^4\equiv 1\pmod 5\) and \(52\equiv 0\pmod 4\), so

\[
2013^{52}\equiv 3^{52}\equiv 1 \pmod 5.
\]

Thus

\[
N\equiv 1+2+1\equiv 4\pmod 5.
\]

So \(5\nmid N\).

---

### 4. Test \(p=7\)

Reduce modulo \(7\):

\[
4^{52}+52^{2013}+2013^{52}.
\]

We have

\[
4^3=64\equiv 1\pmod 7,
\]

and \(52\equiv 1\pmod 3\), so

\[
4^{52}\equiv 4^1\equiv 4\pmod 7.
\]

Next,

\[
52\equiv 3\pmod 7.
\]

The powers of \(3\) modulo \(7\) have period \(6\):

\[
3^6\equiv 1\pmod 7.
\]

Since \(2013\equiv 3\pmod 6\),

\[
52^{2013}\equiv 3^{2013}\equiv 3^3=27\equiv 6\pmod 7.
\]

Finally,

\[
2013\equiv 4\pmod 7,
\]

and since \(4^3\equiv 1\pmod 7\) and \(52\equiv 1\pmod 3\),

\[
2013^{52}\equiv 4^{52}\equiv 4\pmod 7.
\]

Therefore,

\[
N\equiv 4+6+4\equiv 14\equiv 0\pmod 7.
\]

So \(7\mid N\).

Since \(2,3,5\) do not divide \(N\), the smallest prime factor is

\[
\boxed{7}
\]
